item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I liked the overall idea of this SCP. It's nice to find a non-threatening item once in a while.

When I first read it through, though, I was confused - the Special Containment Procedures made me initially believe that this item periodically changes into a different pastry on its own. Then again, this may have been an intentional mislead on part of the author.

When it came to the description, overall it didn't feel too "clinical" in tone to me. For example: "powers" could perhaps be phrased as "effects" or "anomalous properties." The term "birthdayers" actually made me chuckle for a second and broke my willing suspension of disbelief. Perhaps, instead of saying

(termed "birthdayers" for convenience)

You could say

(henceforth referred to as SCP-559-A)

This would give it a more clinical tone, while still retaining the relative harmlessness of the object.

The retrieval log has me jolted even further out of the article. There is no need to expunge the name of the bakery. A simple censorship of a name would work just as well, like ████. Also, the Foundation seems out of character in "convincing" the people to keep it a secret, when standard procedure (from reading the other articles) seems to be the administering of amnesics.

The Addendum feels a little quirky as well.

Overall I enjoy the idea and concept of the article (harmless SCPs are just as entertaining as the scary ones), but the tone is way off. Make it more objective, censor the bakery name rather than expunging it, and make the Foundation more in-character in the retrieval log. I'm not going to vote on this for now. I hope my critique helped.

item.content:encoded:
I know that post was made almost a year ago, but it's the most recent one that actually makes me think about this SCP.

I think "Sliced" should be changed to "Noticeably damaged in any way." So anyone or anything doing something from taking a medium-sized piece off to completely crushing it would cause a transfer, but mice taking a few nibbles of it probably wouldn't do anything.

Better yet, just to make it dangerous and more deserving of its Euclid rating, it should poison anyone or anything attempting to eat it outside of a birthday party. Maybe the lethality can vary based on the age of the person eating it, so it's more forgiving to younger people but pretty lethal to anyone over a certain age.

SCP-559 is a lie
I can't believe no one said it yet.

item.content:encoded:
The transfer of effect makes it just barely over the line, IMO.
It has the potential to leave containment and can't be prevented if triggered, appearing in a new form and location that is impossible to predict. Recontainment would be mind-bendingly difficult if not managed in very short order, such as the scenario in the addendum.

Plus, we don't know what the cake interprets as being sliced. If 682 breaches yet again and steps on it, would that trigger a jump? How about if mice get at it?
